正面:
Handling a Code Mistake
处理代码失误
背面:
Team Lead: I appreciate you reporting this promptly. Hiding mistakes only makes them worse. Can you explain what happened in detail? How severe is the impact, and have you identified the root cause?
You: Absolutely. Yesterday afternoon, I was merging my code for the user profile query API into the main branch. I was in a hurry to finish before the end of the workday and forgot to run the full integration test—only did a quick unit test. The bug is in the SQL query statement: I missed a WHERE clause when joining two tables, which causes the query to return all user data instead of the specific user's data. Right now, it only affects the test environment; the production environment isn't impacted because we haven't deployed the latest code yet.
Team Lead: Good, at least it's not in production. What's your plan to fix it? And how will you prevent this from happening again?
You: I've already identified the error and written the fix— I added the missing WHERE clause and tested it locally; all test cases pass. I'll submit a patch to the main branch in 10 minutes, then run the full integration test to ensure there are no other issues. After that, I'll notify the QA team to retest the user data query function. To prevent this, I'll set a reminder to run full integration tests before every merge, and I'll ask a colleague to do a quick code review for critical modules. I'm truly sorry for the delay this has caused to the test schedule.
Team Lead: That's a solid plan. Taking responsibility and acting quickly is what matters. Make sure you follow through on the prevention measures—code reviews and full tests are non-negotiable for backend development. Keep me updated once the patch is submitted and tested.
You: Thank you for your understanding. I will definitely follow through, and I'll update you as soon as it's done.

正面:
Handling a Technical Incident
处理技术故障事件
背面:
Team Lead: This is critical—our users rely on the platform for daily operations. What's the current status? Have you found any clues about the cause? And how long do you estimate it will take to resolve?
You: We're still in the initial troubleshooting phase. So far, we've checked the server logs and found that the crash was caused by a memory leak in the latest feature we deployed yesterday— the new data processing module is not releasing memory properly, which led to the server running out of memory and crashing. We've temporarily restarted the application server to restore access for users—service should be back up in 5 minutes. However, this is a temporary fix; we need to fix the memory leak to prevent the outage from happening again.
Team Lead: Good, restoring service first is the priority. Assign one member of the team to monitor the server after the restart, and the rest focus on fixing the memory leak. Have you notified the product team to inform users about the temporary outage?
You: Yes, I've already informed the product manager—they're drafting a notification to send to users via email and in-app message, explaining the situation and apologizing for the inconvenience. As for the memory leak fix, our backend developers are reviewing the code for the data processing module now. We estimate we can identify the exact location of the leak in 30 minutes, fix it in an hour, and deploy the patch to production within 2 hours.
Team Lead: Keep me updated every 15 minutes. Once the patch is deployed, run a full load test to ensure the memory leak is completely fixed. Also, after this incident, we need to conduct a root cause analysis and update our deployment process—we should add a load test for new features before deploying to production to catch issues like this early.
You: Understood. I'll send you updates every 15 minutes, and we'll start the root cause analysis once the incident is resolved. We'll also revise the deployment process to include load testing for new modules.
Team Lead: Great. Focus on resolving the incident first—let's minimize the impact on users.
You: Will do.

The main reason is that we encountered some unexpected technical problems: when we were integrating the new interface with the existing system, we found that there are compatibility issues between the two, which took us more time to debug than we anticipated. Second, our team members have agreed to work an extra hour each day this week to make up for the time lost. Team Lead: That's a practical plan. Please keep me updated on the progress every afternoon—if you encounter any other problems, report them to me immediately. Don't hesitate to ask for help if you need it.

课程: L05 Discussing Project Requirements & Technical Feasibility
正面:
Zoom Meeting – Confirming and Analyzing Project Requirements
Zoom 会议：确认并分析项目需求
背面:
Manager: Today's meeting focuses on discussing the new version's core functions. Let's confirm the complete project requirements and sort out the development direction.
You: Okay. According to the product document, the main requirement is to add an automatic data statistics and visual display function. Users can view real-time data charts and export daily, weekly and monthly reports.
Manager: That's correct. The product team hopes to improve data viewing efficiency and reduce manual operation costs. Do you fully understand the business logic and user scenarios behind this requirement?
You: Yes. I have sorted out the whole user operation process and core business logic. However, I still have a few details to clarify. The document does not clearly define the data refresh frequency and the maximum data volume for single export, which may cause ambiguity in later development.
Manager: Good question. The data needs to be refreshed every five minutes, and the single export limit is ten thousand pieces of data.
You: Got it. With these clear rules, we can standardize the interface design and code logic. I will sort out a detailed requirement checklist to ensure no function is missed during development.
Manager: Perfect. Please confirm all uncertain points with the product team in advance to avoid rework in the later stage.
You: Sure, I will complete requirement confirmation before starting technical design.

课程: L05 Discussing Project Requirements & Technical Feasibility
正面:
Discussing Technical Feasibility and Risks
讨论技术可行性与潜在风险
背面:
Manager: After confirming the basic requirements, let's discuss the technical feasibility of this new function. Is it achievable under our current technical architecture?
You: After preliminary technical evaluation, most of the functions are feasible and can be implemented based on our existing framework.
Manager: Are there any technical difficulties or potential risks?
You: Yes. The real-time big data calculation function has certain technical limitations. Our current server configuration and caching strategy cannot support high-frequency data refreshing and large-scale data querying. If we follow the original requirement completely, it may cause system lag, timeout errors and excessive server pressure.
Manager: I see. Do you have any practical solutions or alternative plans?
You: I have two optimization suggestions. First, we can adjust the refresh strategy to balance real-time performance and server pressure. Second, we can split the data query function and adopt asynchronous loading to reduce instantaneous pressure. These adjustments can ensure the core user experience without increasing too much workload.
Manager: That's a reasonable technical solution. We will communicate with the product team to adjust the non-core requirements appropriately.
You: Okay. I will complete the full feasibility report, record all technical risks and corresponding solutions, and submit it before tomorrow's meeting to promote the project progress smoothly.
Manager: Great, please move forward with the technical design.

Tester: The error occurs when users submit forms with special symbols. It works fine with normal input, but triggers an exception with special characters. The test environment runs the latest build released this morning.
You: I understand the problem scenario now. I will simulate this behavior and try to reproduce the bug first. I suspect the front-end data validation rules are incomplete, allowing unfiltered special characters to trigger backend parsing errors.
Tester: That makes sense. This issue has blocked our full regression testing. We need to fix it as soon as possible.
You: Sure. I've gone through the runtime logs and found the problematic code. The existing validation logic lacks checks for special characters. I'll optimize the filtering rules immediately and run regression tests to make sure the issue is fully resolved.
Tester: Great. Please update me once the bug is fixed.
You: No problem. I'll complete the fix within two hours and notify the test team to perform follow-up verification.

You: I've been working on troubleshooting this issue. At this time, the problem cannot be stably reproduced, which complicates debugging.
Manager: Have you analyzed the system logs and monitored data?
You: Yes. I went through the server logs and found that database queries took too long under high-concurrency scenarios. Inefficient SQL caused slow data response time and request timeouts. This is not a crash bug, but a performance bottleneck.
Manager: I see. Do you have a clear solution?
You: Yes. I plan to optimize the fuzzy query SQL and add appropriate indexes to boost query efficiency. In addition, I will adjust the interface timeout threshold to avoid frequent errors. Due to ongoing production risks, a temporary workaround will go live first to reduce user-experience impacts, and the proper fix will be implemented in our next iteration.
Manager: That's a solid arrangement. Please keep the team updated on your debugging progress.
You: Sure. I will continue to monitor the online data, trace the root cause thoroughly, and ensure no similar performance issues happen again.
Manager: Well done. Timely debugging and smooth communication can effectively reduce project risks.

Teammate: I'm a little confused about the caching logic in this payment module. Could you help explain it?
You: Of course. Let me sort out the whole code execution flow for you.
Teammate: I don't mainly understand the trigger conditions of cache update and invalidation.
You: Let's start with the basic logic. This code is divided into two core parts: cache query and cache refresh. When users access the payment page, the program will first query data from the cache. If the cache exists and is within the valid period, it will directly return cached data to improve response speed.
Teammate: I see. What if the cache expires?
You: If the cache is invalid or empty, the program will automatically request data from the database, update the cache synchronously, and reset the valid time. Besides, when users complete payment operations, the code will actively trigger cache invalidation to ensure that the next query can get the latest payment status data.
Teammate: Now I fully understand the call relationship and execution sequence.
You: This set of logic ensures both system response efficiency and data real-time performance. If you need to modify or iterate this function later, you can follow this execution sequence to avoid logical errors.
Teammate: Thanks for your detailed explanation. It helps me a lot with subsequent code maintenance.

Applying for a Professional Skill Training

背面:
You: Good morning, Team Lead. I'd like to talk to you about applying for a professional training program. I recently found an advanced Python development training course that's closely related to our current project, and I think it will help me improve my work efficiency and better complete the backend development tasks.
Team Lead: That's great to hear. We encourage employees to participate in training to improve their skills. Could you tell me more about the training, such as the content, duration, and time arrangement? I need to make sure it won't affect our project progress.
You: Sure. The training is an online course, which lasts for 4 weeks, with 2 hours of learning every evening after work, so it won't take up working time. The content mainly covers advanced Python frameworks, data processing optimization, and bug troubleshooting skills, all of which are exactly what I need for our current project of optimizing the user data processing module.
Team Lead: That sounds perfect, as it won't interfere with our daily work. Is there any cost for this training? And will you be able to apply what you learn to our work after completing the training?
You: The company has a training subsidy policy, right? I checked, and this course is eligible for the subsidy, so I only need to bear 30% of the cost. And yes, I plan to apply the optimization skills I learn to our current project as soon as I finish each module, which can help speed up the data processing and reduce potential bugs.
Team Lead: Great. I approve your application. Please submit the training application form in the company system, and I'll sign it. After completing the training, could you share a brief summary of what you've learned with the team? It might help other colleagues too.
You: Absolutely! Thank you so much for your support. I'll submit the form right away, and I'll definitely share my learning experience with the team after the training.

正面:
Asking About Training Opportunities & Career Development

背面:
You: Hi HR Manager, I hope I'm not disturbing you. I've been working in the company for a year now, and I'd like to ask about the training opportunities available for employees, especially those related to career development and promotion.
HR Manager: Not at all. It's great that you're proactive about your growth. Our company provides a variety of training programs for different levels of employees. For junior employees like you, we have on-the-job training, basic skill workshops, and professional training courses related to your position.
You: That's good to know. I'm particularly interested in training that can help me grow into a senior developer. Could you tell me what training programs are available for that, and how I can apply for them?
HR Manager: Sure. For employees who want to move into senior positions, we have a "Senior Talent Development Program" every quarter. This program includes advanced skill training, project management training, and one-on-one coaching with department leaders. If you wish to apply , you need to have worked in the company for at least one year, have a good performance record, and submit an application form with your career plan.
You: Thank you for the detailed explanation. When will the next program start, and what are the specific requirements for the application? Also, is there any offline training available? I prefer in-person learning because it's easier to interact with teachers and other colleagues.
HR Manager: The next program will start in two months. The specific requirements are listed on the company intranet. You can check there for details. We do have offline training sessions every month, including skill seminars and group discussions. I'll send you the training schedule for the next month, so you can choose the ones that fit your needs.
You: That's very helpful. Thank you so much. I'll check the intranet for the application requirements and look forward to the training schedule.
HR Manager: You're welcome. If you have any other questions about training or career development, feel free to contact me anytime.

正面:
Discussing Performance Evaluation with Team Lead
与组长讨论绩效评估
背面:
You: Good morning, Team Lead. I heard that the quarterly performance evaluation will start next week. I'd like to ask some questions about the evaluation process and standards.
Team Lead: Sure, go ahead. I'm glad you're proactive about this. The evaluation will be conducted from next Monday to Friday, and each employee will have a one-on-one discussion with their direct leader.
You: Thank you for letting me know. Could you tell me what the main evaluation criteria are? I want to make sure I understand how my performance will be rated, especially in terms of project completion and teamwork.
Team Lead: The evaluation has four key criteria: project completion rate, work quality, teamwork, and initiative. For project completion, we'll check if you meet the deadlines and achieve goals; for work quality, we'll look at the accuracy and efficiency of your tasks; teamwork and initiative are also important, such as how well you cooperate with colleagues and whether you take the initiative to solve problems.
You: That's clear. I also want to know if there will be any self-evaluation part? And if so, what should I focus on when filling out the self-evaluation form?
Team Lead: Yes, you need to submit a self-evaluation form before the one-on-one discussion. When filling it out, focus on your achievements in the past quarter, the challenges you faced, your strengths and weaknesses, and your improvement plans for the next quarter. Be specific and provide examples if possible.
You: Understood. Thank you for the detailed explanation. I'll prepare the self-evaluation form carefully and look forward to the discussion with you.
Team Lead: You're welcome. I believe you've done a good job this quarter, and the evaluation will be a good opportunity for us to review your performance and discuss your growth.

正面:
Receiving Performance Feedback & Discussing Improvement
接收绩效反馈并讨论改进
背面:
Team Lead: Let's start our performance evaluation discussion. Overall, your performance this quarter is good. You completed all the assigned projects on time, and your work quality is high. Colleagues also speak highly of your teamwork.
You: Thank you so much. I really appreciate your recognition. I also want to hear your feedback on areas where I can improve. I hope to do better in the next quarter.
Team Lead: That's a good attitude. The main area for improvement is your time management. I noticed that you sometimes spend too much time on small details, which occasionally affects the progress of less urgent tasks. For example, when you were working on the user interface optimization project, you spent extra time adjusting minor details, which delayed the start of the follow-up testing task.
You: I totally agree with you. I've also realized this problem recently. I tend to pursue perfection in every detail, which sometimes leads to inefficiency. Could you give me some suggestions on how to improve my time management?
Team Lead: Sure. I suggest you prioritize your tasks every morning, distinguish between urgent and important tasks, and allocate your time reasonably. You can use time management tools to set deadlines for each task, which will help you focus on the key points and avoid getting stuck on small details. Also, don't hesitate to ask for help if you feel overwhelmed.
You: That's very helpful. Thank you. I'll try this method starting tomorrow and make a conscious effort to improve my time management. I also plan to set clear goals for the next quarter to improve my work efficiency.
Team Lead: Great. I believe you can make progress soon. Let's set a follow-up check in a month to see how you're doing. If you have any questions during this period, feel free to talk to me.
You: Thank you for your guidance and support. I'll work hard to make improvements and live up to your expectations.

正面:
Applying for a Promotion
申请晋升
背面:
You: Good morning, Team Lead. I've been working in the company as a backend developer for two years, and I'd like to discuss the possibility of applying for a promotion to a senior backend developer position. I've prepared a summary of my work achievements and growth over the past two years.
Team Lead: I'm glad you're proactive about your career growth. I've noticed your hard work and progress. You've completed several key projects and helped the team solve many technical problems. Could you share more about why you think you're qualified for this promotion?
You: Thank you for your recognition. Over the past two years, I've mastered advanced backend development skills, led the development of the user data management module, and optimized the system performance, which reduced the response time by 30%. I've also mentored two new developers and helped them quickly adapt to their roles. I believe I have the skills, experience, and responsibility to take on the role of a senior backend developer.
Team Lead: That's a solid performance. The promotion to senior developer requires not only professional skills but also the ability to lead small projects and mentor team members, which you've demonstrated. Do you know the formal promotion process and criteria?
You: I have a basic understanding, but I'd like to confirm. I know I need to submit a promotion application form, go through a performance review, and attend an interview with the department manager. Could you tell me if there are any other specific requirements or things I need to prepare?
Team Lead: You're right about the process. In addition, you need to provide two colleague recommendations and a detailed project report of the key projects you've led. I'll support your application and write a recommendation for you. Submit the application form and related materials to HR next week, and I'll follow up with the department manager.
You: Thank you so much for your support! I'll prepare all the materials this week and submit them on time. I'll continue to work hard and live up to your expectations if I get promoted.
Team Lead: I believe you can do it. Good luck with your application.

正面:
Applying for an Internal Transfer
申请内部转岗
背面:
You: Hi HR Manager, I hope I'm not disturbing you. I've been working in the marketing department as a marketing specialist for a year, and I'd like to apply for an internal transfer to the product department as a product assistant. I'm very interested in product management and have been learning related knowledge in my spare time.
HR Manager: Not at all. Internal transfers are encouraged if they fit your career development and the company's needs. Could you tell me why you want to transfer to the product department, and what relevant skills or experience you have for the product assistant position?
You: Sure. During my work in the marketing department, I often communicated with the product team to understand user needs and product functions, which made me realize my interest in product management. I've learned product design basics and user research methods through online courses, and I've helped the product team collect and sort user feedback several times. I'm detail-oriented, good at communication, and I believe these skills are suitable for the product assistant role.
HR Manager: That's good to know. The product department is currently looking for a product assistant, so your application couldn't come at a better time. Do you have any questions about the product assistant position, such as job responsibilities or work requirements?
You: Yes, I'd like to ask about the main responsibilities of the product assistant and whether there will be any training for the new role. I want to make sure I can adapt to the new position quickly. HR
Manager: The main responsibilities include collecting user feedback, assisting the product manager with product planning, organizing product meetings, and updating product documents. We will provide a one-month on-the-job training to help you adapt to the role, and you'll have a mentor from the product team to guide you.
You: That's reassuring. Thank you. What's the next step for the transfer application? Do I need to get approval from my current department manager first?
HR Manager: Yes, you need to discuss it with your current department manager and get their approval first. Then submit the internal transfer application form to me, and I'll coordinate with the product department to arrange an interview. If the interview is successful, we'll finalize the transfer date.
You: Understood. Thank you so much for your help. I'll discuss it with my department manager today and submit the application form as soon as possible.
HR Manager: You're welcome. If you have any other questions during the process, feel free to contact me.
